record.reason: verifier FAIL: value reproduces most of its own evidence window

provenance: M40 cold review, three findings folded into one case because they are one property: the surface must end TERMINAL and USABLE however the run ends, and each defect instead left it asserting something untrue. (1) `es.onerror` polled `GET /tasks/{id}` with no `.catch`, and `renderResult` read `r.status.split(':')` unguarded -- so a run record that 404s (the in-memory `RUNS` after a redeploy, support-matrix D19, or a mid-run restart, D18) threw a TypeError, and `$('go').disabled = false` never ran. (2) The same handler re-enabled submission and rendered against the module-global `runId`, so a late poll for run A built `/runs/<B>/step_N.png` URLs -- run B's screenshots under run A's step captions, no error anywhere. (3) `renderScraped` cut a value at 300 chars with no marker, which on the dominant live failure shape (D28's CONTAINER DUMP, six finance domains) renders a multi-thousand-character page dump as a tidy, well-scoped extraction, hiding the exact defect the run was rejected for. What makes (1) an M40 defect rather than an old one is the spinner this milestone added: the page now ANIMATES the claim that a dead run is in progress. The case drives the real PAGE on the shared `_ui_page` render with `fetch` and `EventSource` stubbed, the same way `ui-form` does, and restores both. ROUND 2 (same milestone, second cold review) widened this case three times, each against a defect the first version could not see. (a) `lost()` was called for a run record that still said `running` — a stream dropped by a proxy idle timeout or a sleeping laptop over a run that is alive and usually succeeds seconds later — painting `#status` in the failure colour and `#progress[data-terminal]=failure`. That is the same lie as the spinner over a dead run, pointed the other way and worse, because the run's real result is then never shown; `detached()` replaces it, asserts no verdict and sets no `data-terminal`. (b) The `smoke()` stream kept its own handle and its own `onerror`, so the exact spinner-over-a-dead-run defect this case was written for stayed open on the button beside the fixed one. (c) The stale-poll assertion was VACUOUS: it let the poll land before reassigning `runId` and then compared `#status` with itself, so deleting both cross-run guards kept it green. It now holds the poll open across the reassignment and asserts the old run's record never reaches `#result`, its screenshots never reach `#pvshot`, and it does not release the buttons under the run that now owns them.

triage.watched_red: against `git show HEAD:src/browser/server.py` served by uvicorn and driven by the same stubs: submit -> stream 500 -> record 404 gives `#status` 'RUNNING' with `go.disabled true` forever and one uncaught pageerror, "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'split')". Re-run against the fixed page: `#status` 'STREAM LOST', `animationName` 'none', both buttons enabled, `#progress[data-terminal]` 'failure', no pageerror. The clip half was watched red the same way -- a 2000-char value rendered as 300 characters with no ellipsis and no length. Round 2, each watched red against the round-1 page: the `running` record gave `terminal: 'failure'` with `status_class: 'big failure'`; deleting the `runId !== mine` guards with the poll held open rendered run A's `STALE-ANSWER-FROM-RUN-A` into `#result` under run B; and `smoke()`'s stream erroring left `#status` `running` with `animationName: spin`.
triage.note: Ceilings, declared. This grades the page's handlers against a stubbed transport, not a real dropped connection against the real gateway. `/smoke/stream`'s SERVER half — the `SEM.locked()` early return — is graded by nothing here, and that guard is a READ, not an acquire: two tabs both starting a browser check still launch two Chromiums, and `/readyz` reports neither. That is logged as debt, not fixed behind this case's back.
